thread:
Nadia: Quick brain-dump: proposing a 'Cohort Confidence Estimator' (CCE) that runs alongside canary/A-B traffic to smooth decision signals and add hysteresis before automatic fallback triggers. Goal: reduce rollback churn from transient signal noise.
Carlos: neat name. how does CCE differ from simply increasing thresholds or adding cooldown timers?
Nadia: three differences: 1) CCE fuses multiple orthogonal signals (latency, error-rate, queue depth, model loss/regressions) into a short-lived confidence score; 2) it provides a time-aware hysteresis (confidence decay + reinforcement) rather than fixed cooldowns; 3) it's cohort-aware so different tenants/models get different priors.
Priya: what signals are we fusing exactly? need to keep it cheap.
Nadia: base signals: p95 latency delta, error-rate delta, deploy-sidebackpressure events, recent fallback counts, and a lightweight quality-signal from evals (if available). Each signal is normalized and weighted; output is a confidence value 0..1.
sre-bot: note: INF-2111 created for CCE metrics + alerting integration.
Carlos: runtime placement? inside proxy, sidecar, or separate service?
Nadia: prefer a hybrid: local estimator in the proxy/sidecar for low-latency scoring (windowed to 5-30s) and a central aggregator that smooths region/cohort-wide view (for longer-term decisions). Local score is used for immediate hysteresis; central score informs global rollouts.
Priya: decision API change? we already have a fallback controller.
Nadia: minimal contract: fallback-controller accepts `cohort_confidence` and `confidence_window_ms`. If `cohort_confidence < threshold` and sustained for `decay_window`, trigger fallback. But confidence also supports a 'reinforce' signal: if confidence rises quickly, we can back off a rollback.
Carlos: how to avoid gaming the score (false positives due to noisy metrics)?
Nadia: add adversarial-resistant features: require at least two orthogonal signals to deviate concurrently for a fast drop in confidence. Single-signal blips cause only transient dips that decay slowly. Also cap impact from any single signal.
Priya: ops concerns: memory and metric cardinality. Cohorts can be many.
Nadia: design: use streaming aggregates and fixed-size circular buffers keyed by (cohort, model-class). No per-request storage. Metrics summarized to counts/quantiles. Central aggregator receives periodic summaries, not raw events.
sre-bot: ops note: recommend retention policy for CCE telemetry as 14d short-term + 90d coarse.
Carlos: tradeoffs? added complexity to rollout logic. Could hide root cause if confidence opaque.
Nadia: agree. require that CCE emits explainability metadata: top-2 contributing signals and their deltas in the webhook when a fallback decision is made. UI will show 'confidence drivers'.
Priya: fail-open or fail-closed?
Nadia: fail-open. If estimator is unreachable, fallback-controller reverts to legacy heuristics and emits an incident. Never reduce availability.
Carlos: rollout plan?
Nadia: prototype as library in proxy, opt-in via feature-flag per-route. Stage: (1) dev-only with synthetic traffic, (2) sidecar on internal endpoints (1% cohorts) for 1 week, (3) US-regional canary at 5% for 2 weeks, (4) global 50% with opt-in.
Priya: important to get UX right in Console: show confidence timeline, contributing signals, and an explanation for any automated fallbacks. Ops needs an override kill-switch.
Nadia: will draft RFC with sequence diagrams, proto schema for `cohort_confidence` payload, and sample explain metadata. Quick example payload: `{"cohort_confidence":"0.34","window_ms":"30000","top_drivers":["p95_latency:+28%","error_rate:+0.7%"]}`
Carlos: love the explainability bit. small ask: make thresholds per-model-class and allow auto-tuning based on historical data.
Nadia: noted. auto-tune as future work; initial release will be config-driven. I'll ping @eng-sre for the runbook and @product for Console wireframes. :spiral_note_pad:
